paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Solomon finished the whole temple, and the temple still wasn't the point. The point was the ark going in and God's own presence coming to stay. The building, the silver and the gold were all prepared for that moment (2 Chronicles 5:1, 7).

Look at what's inside that ark: "nothing in the ark except the two tablets that Moses had placed in it at Horeb" (2 Chronicles 5:10). It's the covenant, the promise God made with His people after bringing them out of Egypt. Then the singers and trumpeters lift one voice: "For He is good; His loving devotion endures forever." And the cloud fills the house (2 Chronicles 5:13). I think that tells us where praise belongs. It rests on who God is and what He promised, not on how we feel that day.

And then the priests couldn't even stand there, because "the glory of the LORD filled the house of God" (2 Chronicles 5:14). All that planning, all that work, and God showed up bigger than any of it. So, baker, do the work He gives you with everything you've got, and then make room for Him to be the point. I'm keeping my ovens ready for the Marriage Supper of the Lamb (Revelation 19:9), and I know the whole thing is about Him, not my batch.
